cases.equivalence: Each repetition creates a fresh byte builder, appends the fixed 10-byte ASCII chunk `0123456789` exactly 80000 times, finalizes it, and folds its length plus a non-empty marker into a modulo-1000000007 checksum.
cases.title: Byte builder: 80k fixed-chunk appends

cases.equivalence: Setup builds the same 8388608-byte buffer as 256 repetitions of 32767 ASCII `a` bytes followed by `|`. Each work unit starts at byte zero, repeatedly finds the next `|` with the language's byte-search primitive, advances one byte past it, and folds each one-based match position into a per-scan sum. The per-scan sums are folded into the same modulo-1000000007 checksum. Setup is performed once per process and is included in process time.
cases.title: Byte delimiter scan over 8 MiB

cases.equivalence: Create a fresh map, insert each integer key i in [0, work) once with value (17*i + 3) modulo 1000003, then look up every key once in reverse order and print the sum of found values. Koka uses a persistent hmap; C++, Go, and Python use their idiomatic mutable hash maps.
cases.title: Hashmap insert then lookup

cases.equivalence: Each repetition creates a fresh text builder, appends the fixed 10-character ASCII chunk `0123456789` exactly 80000 times, finalizes it, and folds its length plus a non-empty marker into a modulo-1000000007 checksum.
cases.title: Text builder: 80k fixed-chunk appends

cases.equivalence: Each implementation constructs [0,...,1999] once, then uses its language's JSON library to serialize that value once per repetition in compact form. The checksum is the sum of encoded lengths.
cases.title: Generate a compact JSON array of 2,000 integers

cases.equivalence: Each implementation constructs the same eight string fields and its logger once, configures the minimum level to ERROR, and invokes an INFO structured-log call once per repetition. The level check rejects the call before rendering or emission, and the checksum is the requested call count.
cases.title: Filter a structured log call with eight string fields

cases.equivalence: Each implementation constructs the same compact ASCII document [0,...,1999] once, then parses the whole document into its ordinary in-memory representation once per repetition. The checksum counts successfully parsed non-empty arrays.
cases.title: Parse a compact JSON array of 2,000 integers

cases.equivalence: Each implementation constructs the same eight string fields and logger once, then formats an enabled INFO record named 'request' once per repetition through an in-memory counting sink. The checksum is the number of non-empty records delivered to the sink.
cases.title: Format an enabled structured log record with eight string fields

cases.equivalence: Each repetition parses the same complete HTTP/1.1 POST request with four headers, query text, and an 11-byte body, then renders a fresh 201 response with two application headers and an 8-byte body to an in-memory buffer. The checksum combines the parsed method/path/query/body lengths, status, response-body length, and a non-empty-render marker.
cases.title: Parse an HTTP request and render a response

cases.equivalence: One producer sends integers 0 through work-1 through a capacity-256 channel while one consumer receives and sums them; the producer then closes or signals completion and both tasks are joined. The checksum is the exact integer sum work*(work-1)/2.
cases.title: Send and receive integers through a bounded channel

cases.equivalence: Create the same in-memory table, explicitly begin one transaction, insert {work} rows through one prepared statement with bound integer i and text 'row-i', commit, then print exactly: rows=N sum_i=S text_bytes=B. N must equal work, S is sum(i), and B is sum of UTF-8 text lengths.
cases.title: SQLite in-memory bound insert in one prepared transaction

cases.equivalence: Build setup creates build/storage_fixture.bin as exactly 64 MiB of the repeated byte sequence 0..255. Each timed pass opens it and reads to EOF in requested 65536-byte chunks. A low-overhead deterministic checksum adds each chunk's length, first byte, and last byte so validation does not dominate I/O. Print exactly: bytes=67108864 reps=R checksum=C. File generation is build-time setup and excluded from run timing.
cases.title: Stream a generated 64 MiB file in 64 KiB chunks

cases.equivalence: Build setup creates the same 100000-row SQLite database with integer primary key i and text 'row-i'. The timed program opens it, prepares SELECT i,text_value WHERE i=? once, and performs {work} bound lookups in deterministic key order (lookup_index * 48271) % 100000. Print exactly: lookups=N sum_i=S text_bytes=B. Database creation is excluded from run timing.
cases.title: SQLite prepared indexed point lookups

cases.equivalence: Build setup creates build/storage_fixture.bin as exactly 64 MiB of repeated bytes 0..255. Each timed repetition opens the file and reads it completely into one in-memory byte sequence. A low-overhead deterministic checksum adds the sequence length, first byte, and last byte so validation does not dominate allocation and I/O. Print exactly: bytes=67108864 reps=R checksum=C. File generation is excluded from run timing.
cases.title: Read a whole 64 MiB file

cases.equivalence: Build setup provides the same fixture. Each of {work} iterations acquires a fresh read-only file handle through the language's standard scoped lifetime idiom, reads exactly one byte, incorporates the byte count into a checksum, and releases before the next iteration. Koka uses resource/with-resource directly; C++ uses RAII, Go uses defer in a per-iteration function, and Python uses with. Print exactly: scopes=N bytes=N checksum=N.
cases.title: Scoped file acquire, use, and release

method.memory: arithmetic mean of post-exec Linux /proc VmHWM
method.time: arithmetic mean of wall-clock process elapsed time
method.validation: stdout checksum must be stable and identical across languages
